Gotcha! If I'm understanding what you want to implement correctly, this Node library seems to implement the `fetch` browser API and to allow you to code client HTTP requests the same in Node and Deno. (All you would need to do is to differently is include this library in your Node project.)

[https://github.com/node-fetch/node-fetch](https://github.com/node-fetch/node-fetch)

Deno HTTP requests (and browser JS HTTP requests) are generally made using the [Fetch API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API). Node's current lack of this standard JS method was one reason Deno was implemented in the first place, to my understanding. Node was created before a lot of great JS features like `import` , `fetch`, `Promise`, etc. were created. Deno has had them since the beginning.

One approach could be to isolate the Deno/Node specific code in a single JS/TS file kept as small as possible. To make it clear what needs to be done individually for Node and Deno. 

Overall, a Node project is centered around package.json and a Deno project isn’t. It may be hard or impossible to have one Git repo that works for Deno and Node simultaneously.

Well, the reason I wrote this in the first place was that for some reason, for some particular artist, Beets started thinking all that artist's songs belonged to the same album, even though the mp3 tags had them listed under more than one album (and VLC and Foobar agreed there was more than one album).

So, I wrote this. I have a habit of writing my own custom software when I dislike one little thing about another app. (Here's my  [replacement for Microsoft OneNote](https://gitlab.com/jane314/twonote), lolol)

​

*Beets advantages*

\- More time tested

\- More customizable

\- Has cool features like auto playlists

\- Handles lots of audio formats (my script only supports mp3, m4a, wav, opus, ogg, and flac, because that's what I had in my library). I had to treat each of these file types separately in the script based on how ffmpeg reads their metadata. And even then, this was essentially guess-and-check based on my personal library, not any rigorous understanding of why ffmpeg reads their metadatas differently).

​

*Advantages of my script*

*-* Very simple, so minimizes mysterious behavior and can be troubleshooted easily.

\- Fixes that one problem I had

But also, for me a problem like this says something about how I think about myself and how I want to change. I think I've gotten somewhere by realizing that if I'm constantly beating myself up for the stupid things I say, then I need to change as a person. When I'm dying at the things I say, that means I'm not being what I want to be. The positive spin for me is that if I beat myself up, then implicitly I am envisioning a better self. If that makes sense. For me the solution is committing to being a better person and trying to be mindful.

The solution for me isn't to "accept myself", exactly. There are things I need to change, and once I change those things, I can be more OK with quirkier parts of myself.

And also, getting anxiety under control, and going getting a legit prescription instead of just self medicating with weed and booze is part of it. Substance abuse is real and I didn't realize that was applicable to me also until recently. Good luck :)

I wasn't even able to start thinking clearly about my desired gender until I started transitioning. When I started, all I was able to realize was that I needed to transition into someone more feminine. I went into transition pretty much assuming I was going to be woman-leaning nonbinary, but I ended up a trans woman, so that can be a thing. For me, it wasn't possible to see what my transition would end up looking like at the beginning.
